label: Deactivate triggers
description: Turn off triggers (park, hibernate or wipe): the program's own, or with `instance` that instance's per-instance triggers, with `running` deciding what happens to the runs they fired that are still going.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: Whose triggers: an instance id your program gives it (`user-42`), for that instance's per-instance triggers. Unwired: the program's own triggers, the ones shared by every instance. Wired, and no id arrives (the step feeding it did not run): this node skips.

inputs.name: only
inputs.description: Only these triggers, named as the program writes them. Unwired: all of them (every shared trigger, or every per-instance trigger of the instance).

inputs.name: triggers
inputs.label: Triggers
inputs.description: Park keeps everything that arrives (answers, events, the trigger's own fires) and runs it once the trigger is back, while a caller on a route is told to try again in a moment; hibernate does the same for `graceMinutes` with its questions hidden, then takes nothing more; wipe drops it all.

inputs.name: running
inputs.label: Running work
inputs.description: The runs they fired that are still going: wait lets them finish, cancel stops them. `wipe` needs cancel.

inputs.name: graceMinutes
inputs.label: Grace minutes
inputs.description: Hibernate only: how long it keeps accepting.

inputs.name: includeSelf
inputs.label: Stop this run too
inputs.description: On: this run is cancelled too when it is one of the runs reached.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the triggers are down; under `running: wait` their runs may still be finishing.

then.message: DeactivateTriggers '{id}' names {names} in `only`, which is no per-instance trigger of this program. It is given an `instance`, so it acts on that instance's triggers: name each the way the program writes it (`inbox`, `work.inbox` inside a group, or `one.inbox` inside an included file), or leave `instance` unwired to act on the program's own triggers.

DeactivateTriggers '{id}' names {names} in `only`, which is no shared trigger of this program. It has no `instance`, so it acts on the program's own triggers: name each the way the program writes it (`inbox`, `work.inbox` inside a group, or `one.inbox` inside an included file), or wire `instance` to act on an instance's per-instance triggers.
DeactivateTriggers '{id}' wipes the triggers but lets running work finish. Wiping drops what the runs still need, so set `running` to cancel, or pick park or hibernate for `triggers`.
